# Markdown renderer doesn't handle special link cases correctly

I'm using mistune's MarkdownRenderer and noticed that it doesn't properly handle several link formatting cases.

## Steps to reproduce:

1. Create a markdown document with various link formats
2. Parse and render it using the MarkdownRenderer

## Current behavior:

The renderer doesn't correctly handle several link cases:

1. Links with URLs containing parentheses aren't properly escaped
2. Auto-links (where the text is the same as the URL) aren't rendered as `<url>` format
3. Email auto-links aren't properly handled
4. Reference-style links with labels aren't working

## Example:

```python
from mistune import create_markdown
from mistune.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

md = create_markdown(renderer=MarkdownRenderer())

# This doesn't render correctly
text = "Here's a [link](https://example.com/page(1))"
result = md(text)
print(result)  # Should escape the parentheses in the URL

# Auto-links don't work
text = "[https://example.com](https://example.com)"
result = md(text)
print(result)  # Should be <https://example.com>

# Email links don't work
text = "[user@example.com](mailto:user@example.com)"
result = md(text)
print(result)  # Should be <user@example.com>

# Reference-style links don't work
text = "[link][ref]\n\n[ref]: https://example.com"
result = md(text)
print(result)  # Should maintain the reference format
```

I think this is happening because the link renderer is missing some special case handling for these different link formats. The current implementation seems to be treating all links the same way.
